html:
The kingdom of Gala was the realm of the Massylii, the Berber people of eastern Numidia, in what is now northeastern Algeria. Its capital was Cirta, today's Constantine. It is shown here in 200 BCE.

Gala, also written Gaia, was king during the Second Punic War and an ally of Carthage. His son was Masinissa. When Gala died, around 206 BCE, the throne was fought over, and the western king of the Masaesyli took the land. Masinissa went over to Rome, won it back with Scipio's help, and after Carthage's defeat in 202 BCE ruled a united Numidia.
